fixes.explanation: Water it is, friend. The LORD tells Jeremiah, the prophet, to put the loincloth around his waist, “…but do not let it touch water.” (Jeremiah 13:1) Linen that has to stay away from water. I can't keep flour off my apron for ten minutes, so I'm impressed.

Oil isn't mentioned anywhere in this command. The LORD tells Jeremiah, the prophet, to wear the loincloth but “…do not let it touch water.” (Jeremiah 13:1) Oil is welcome all over my kitchen, but this linen gets a different rule. The word here is water.

True. Jeremiah says, “So I bought a loincloth in accordance with the word of the LORD, and I put it around my waist.” (Jeremiah 13:2) Strange orders, and he did it just as the LORD said. I think a lot of us would have at least raised an eyebrow, and I have a LOT of eyebrow.

The rocks, yes. The LORD says to hide the loincloth “…in a crevice of the rocks.” (Jeremiah 13:4) A crack in the rocks at Perath. Not the back of a junk drawer, where I spent years, and believe me, I know the difference.

Faded would be a gentle ending, but the text is harsher. Jeremiah, the prophet, digs it up and finds “…it was ruined…” and of no use at all. (Jeremiah 13:7) Of no use at all is a long way from fine to wear.
The pride, that's it. The LORD says, “…I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 13:9) The ruined loincloth was a picture of that.
The harvest isn't what the LORD names here. He says, “…I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 13:9) The thing being ruined is their pride.
Walls aren't mentioned in this verse. The LORD says, “…I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 13:9) The word to catch is pride.
Nations don't appear in this verse. The LORD says these people “…go after other gods to serve and worship them…” (Jeremiah 13:10) Gods is what the verse says they go after.

The text says the opposite, friend. The LORD says He made them cling to Him, “But they did not listen.” (Jeremiah 13:11) That's the sad end of the verse. The verse says He made them cling, and it ends with that line.

That's the reply. The LORD says they will reply, “Don’t we surely know that every wineskin should be filled with wine?” (Jeremiah 13:12) That sounds like the look we've all given somebody explaining the obvious.

Nobody's calling for wine in this verse. The LORD says they will reply, “Don’t we surely know that every wineskin should be filled with wine?” (Jeremiah 13:12) They'd be saying they already know it. No refills requested.
Empty wineskins don't come up here. The LORD says they will reply, “Don’t we surely know that every wineskin should be filled with wine?” (Jeremiah 13:12) They'd be saying they know this already.

False, and the verse names them. The LORD says He will fill with drunkenness “…all who live in this land—the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 13:13) This part of the passage is heavy, and nobody is skipped.
